description:
HushTumblr v0.0.10: 55 patches for Tumblr 47.0.0.108, which needs Android 8 or newer. It moves to Tumblr 47.0.0.108 on Morphe patcher 2.3.0 and adds nine patches. New switches hide your own reblogs and posts you've liked, collapse long posts and share a video's direct link. Dark background color now reaches blog and tag pages and can follow your wallpaper, and the bundle is signed. Validation: 1244 runtime tests passed. All 314 patch tests passed. All 55 patches applied without forcing to Tumblr 47.0.0.108. Needs Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer. The .mpp is a patch bundle, not a Tumblr APK. Uninstall the stock app first, then sign in with your email and a Tumblr password.

### What's new

* The patches move from 46.8.1.100 to Tumblr 47.0.0.108, the newest release. Every patch applies to it, so that's the version to patch.
* The bundle is built on Morphe patcher 2.3.0 now, the one that comes with Morphe Manager 2.5.0 and Morphe Desktop 2.1.0. Update Manager to 2.5.0 or newer before you add this release, since older Manager builds can't load it.
* Dark background color now reaches blog and tag pages. Those pages paint their owner's color, so a cream blog or a teal tag used to show through the gaps between black posts. A blog's title or link color that wouldn't show on the new background turns white or near black. The screens where you edit your own blog's colors still show the real ones.
* New **Line between posts** switch on the Interface page, off by default. It draws a thin line in the gap between posts, so it's easier to see where one ends on a black background.
* New **Hide Featured posts** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes out the posts Tumblr's staff push into your dashboard under a Featured header. A post goes only when Tumblr marks it both ways, with the Featured icon and the menu choice Tumblr gives its own promotions, so a regular post with a similar header stays. Quick setups' Quiet choice turns it on too.
* New **Hide your own reblogs** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes the reblogs you made out of your dashboard, so you don't scroll past your own reblogs between the posts of people you follow. The rest of Tumblr still shows them, your blog and a post you open by itself included.
* New **Hide liked posts** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes posts you've already liked out of your dashboard, so the ones that come back around don't cost you scrolling. A post you like while it's on screen stays put until the feed loads it again. Everywhere else still shows them, so a liked post you open from a link or a notification is still there.
* A post you open by itself, from a link or a notification, now loads with Hide reblogs or Hide posts with words on. Those switches clear a feed, so they took out the very post you asked for and the page stayed empty. The same post in a feed later is still hidden as usual.
* New **Match my wallpaper** switch under Dark background color, off by default. On Android 12 or newer it takes the dark background from your wallpaper's colors, so there's no color code to pick when patching. A new wallpaper shows after Tumblr restarts.
* New **Share video links** switch on the Posts page, off by default. Long-press a video in a post and you can share its direct link or copy it. Before, a long press on a video did nothing at all. The same menu can also save the video into your Downloads folder, with a toast once it's in. Android 10 and newer don't ask for storage access for that. Android 8 and 9 ask first, and the save starts by itself once you allow it.
* New **Sharper images** switch on the Posts page, off by default. Tumblr loads photos in posts at 640 pixels across at most, and smaller on a slow connection, so they look soft on most phones. With the switch on, a photo loads from the larger copy Tumblr already keeps, up to twice the width it's shown at (usually the 1280 one), and a slow connection gets the same copy. It uses more data. GIFs go up too, but never past the pixel count of a 1280 by 960 one, since a playing GIF keeps a few frames in memory. Very large photos stay capped as well.
* New **Collapse long posts** switch on the Posts page, off by default. A long post can take several screens of scrolling. With the switch on, a post longer than about a screen gets cut in your timelines with Tumblr's own Read more row under it, the same one you see when an author cuts their post. Tap it and the whole post opens right where it is in the timeline, so you don't lose your place, and it stays open as you scroll on. That holds on tag pages too, where Tumblr fades long posts out by itself, so the post you opened isn't cut again there. A post Tumblr always cuts still opens on its own page. A post that runs only a little over stays whole. A long entry in a reblog trail gets cut the same way, and its Read more opens the post on its own page like an author's cut does. Asks keep Tumblr's layout. The **Collapsed post length** row under the switch moves the cut to about half a screen or two screens with a tap, and a settings file carries your pick.
* New **Sanitize sharing links** switch on the Privacy page, on by default. Tumblr adds `?source=share` to the post and blog links you share or copy, which tells it the visit came from a share. With the switch on, the link goes out without that tag and still opens the same post. A link is otherwise left exactly as Tumblr made it. Quick setups' Privacy choice turns it on too.
* Hide ads now takes sponsored banners out of your feeds too, the takeover banners a sponsor pays for and the Sponsored Day ones. Tumblr's own banners without a sponsor, like Answer Time, stay. When a sponsor has paid for the header at the top of Explore, that header stays empty instead, the same as when it doesn't load, so its takeover ad can't open from it.
* New **App font** patch, off by default. Turn it on under Interface and Tumblr's own font gives way to your phone's, or to a .ttf or .otf file you pick there. Fonts a post's author picked stay as they are, and a change shows after a restart.
* Flipping a switch near the bottom of a settings page doesn't make the page jump anymore, so a second tap in the same spot can't land on the switch next to the one you meant. Two things moved it. The restart row appearing above slid the list down, and while a switch saved, its shorter "Saving the setting" line let the rows above drop into the gap and stay there.
* Hide the Follow button now reaches the reblog trail too. Each blog quoted in a reblog has its own header with a Follow button, and those kept showing while the one at the top of the post was gone.
* The patch bundle is signed now. Morphe Manager shows "Signed by 0859 9c9b 1bd2 9cac" on the HushTumblr source and remembers that key, so a later bundle signed with any other key, or not signed at all, gets refused instead of loaded.
* Hide ads now also turns off the full-screen ad Tumblr can show when you open a blog, whether you get there from the dashboard, a reblog, a notification or a message. The pause Tumblr keeps between those ads is left alone, since switching it off would only take the pause away.
* When something in HushTumblr settings can't finish, what to do next now stays under the row you tapped. It used to be a toast that faded after a few seconds, and Android 12 and later show only two lines of one, so large text got cut off. This covers links no app can open, Android's app settings not opening, switches and tab moves that didn't save, a Resume or Quick setup that didn't run, font files that couldn't be used and refused exports or imports. The diagnostic report and **Clear diagnostic data** rows work the same way now, so the folder a full report went to stays readable. A link you can't open comes with a Copy link button.
* A failed tab move or import keeps what you tried, so trying again picks up where it stopped. The import preview also gets a **Choose another file** button for when the file itself was the problem. Notes under rows come back when Android rebuilds the screen (say, after you rotate the phone), and a result that lands after you've closed settings or switched apps shows under its row once you're back. One that lands while the screen is being rebuilt shows on the new one, and one for a row on another settings page waits there until you open it. Hiding Quick setups says right under that page's row where to get it back. A Tab order tap while a change is still saving opens the list once the save is done instead of doing nothing.
* A settings page opened with a keyboard or D-pad starts at the top again. The "HushTumblr is paused" line used to sit just above the view, so the switches under it read as on.
* With a keyboard, D-pad or mouse, the settings home page comes back where you left it after Back or a cleared search, even when a section heading or the status card sat at the top. It used to land one row further down, with that heading pushed out of view.
* A switch, font file or Quick setup that waits for a restart now says so right under that row. The note goes once you undo that change or nothing's waiting anymore, and a change the next start makes anyway (Pause while safe mode already pauses) doesn't get one. Screen readers read it once from there, and again only if you go back to it. The Tab order list shows "Saving changes" under it while a slow save runs, then where the tab went and whether Tumblr needs a restart, and the dialog keeps its size while those come and go. Android 16 is phasing out the pop-up announcements these used, and those were gone the moment they were spoken.
* Hide ads now keeps Tumblr's ad networks (Google Mobile Ads, Meta Audience Network, Vungle and Nimbus) from starting when Tumblr launches. They woke up at every cold start and wrote their files before any HushTumblr switch was read. Disable analytics does the same for LiveRamp's identity tracker. Turn either switch off, or pause HushTumblr, and they start again after a restart.
* With Hide hashtags on, a Tumblr TV video whose only text was its tags doesn't keep a lone "... more" under the blog name anymore. Tapping it opened nothing. A video with a description still gets its label.
* With Hide note counts on, each comment in a post's notes drops its own like and reply counts too, and TalkBack doesn't read them out either. The Reply and like buttons still work.
* New **Keep Blaze posts** option under Hide ads on the Feed page, off by default. With it on, posts someone paid to promote with Blaze stay in your dashboard while network ads and other sponsored cards still go. Your word and post type filters still apply to those posts.
* The Words to hide and Allowed words editors can test your list on a made-up post now. Type some post text, trail text, tags or a summary under **Try it on a post** and it tells you whether the word filter would hide that post. It names the word that did it and where it was, or the allowed word that kept the post. It uses the same whole-word matching and the same Match switches as your dashboard, and tags work typed with commas or the way a post shows them (#art #cats). Nothing typed there is saved, and it's empty again each time you open the editor.
* With **Mute posts locally** on, a post's menu on the dashboard can also hide one blog's reblogs or its originals. A reblog offers "Hide reblogs from" that blog and an original offers "Hide originals from" it, so you can keep someone's own posts while their reblogs go, or the other way around. The rule only works on your dashboard and its tabs. Explore, their blog page and search still show those posts, and so does a post you open by itself. It goes in the same private list as your muted posts, for this account only, and Manage muted posts shows it as its own row you can tap to remove. A post Tumblr doesn't say enough about to tell which kind it is always stays.
* Disable analytics now really keeps Crashlytics crash reports off. The patch already set Firebase's manifest flag for that, but Tumblr turns crash collection back on by itself every time it starts, and its call wins over the flag. With the switch on, that call now leaves collection off. Turn the switch off, or pause HushTumblr, and Tumblr's own setting is back after a restart.
* The README's Help explains how to keep a patched copy next to your regular Tumblr with Morphe's Clone app patch. You sign in to the copy with your email and it keeps its own HushTumblr settings, but `Fix push notifications` only covers the regular app.

### Behind the scenes

* **Tooling:** The check that every GitLab mirror in a source notice still answers doesn't fail anymore when GitLab says "too many requests". It spaces its requests out, waits as long as GitLab asks (a minute at most) and tries again, so only a mirror that's really gone fails it.
* **Tooling:** The build runs on Gradle 9.8.2 with Gson 2.15.0, Guava 33.8.0 and Commons Lang 3.21.0. None of them fixes a known advisory here, so it's upkeep. The release check accepts the 9.8.2 wrapper now.
* **Tooling:** Device runs don't stop anymore when another session happens to read the shared lease file at the same moment. Opening or releasing the lease waits a few seconds and tries again, and a missing lease or one someone else holds still stops the run.
* **Tooling:** The source census reads ReVanced's GitLab mirror in three GraphQL questions now. Over REST it took a request for every branch and watched path, 70 of them for that mirror's 35 branches, and GitLab allows an address with no token about 60 an hour. Each comparison is asked once a run too. Forks that GitLab has renamed while they wait to be deleted stay out of the census, because a scanner keeps making and deleting them faster than any census could record them.
* **Tooling:** A release walk now waits for Android's verifier to finish on both the clean reference and the exact build that got installed, and both files have to hash the same before and after it runs. Publishing refuses evidence that's old or partial. It also refuses evidence that doesn't match, down to one verifier message too many or too few.
* **Tooling:** A release walk now checks each required destination instead of trusting its screen count. Login screens, wrong search results, duplicate or missing routes, recorded problems and invalid timestamps can't earn a full PASS. Shorter exploratory walks remain partial.
* **Tooling:** Release walks now prove which APK was installed. Patch runs keep the input, bundle, patch selection and signing identity beside the signed output. The walker checks the installed bytes before and after its run, and publishing refuses evidence that's missing or doesn't match this build.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/walk-app.ps1` scrolls the Hush settings list with slow drags now, down first and then back up, and stops once the list stops moving. Quick swipes flung the list past rows that slid under its pinned header, so a walk on a phone could miss settings pages that were there all along.
* **Tooling:** `scripts/patch-for-device.ps1` can now sign a gate run it reuses with the BKS key Morphe makes. Plain `apksigner.bat` can't open that keystore, so the script falls back to apksigner's own jar with BouncyCastle loaded. When both fail, the error shows what each one said.
* **Tooling:** Changelog entries don't open with a "Tumblr:" label anymore. HushTumblr only patches Tumblr, so it repeated itself on every line. The release scripts stopped adding or asking for it, and drop it from any bullet that still has one when a release is cut.
* **Tooling:** The build signs the bundle when `MORPHE_SIGNING_KEY` holds the private key, and refuses a key that isn't the one `morphe-signing.pub` publishes. Without it the build still works and says the bundle is unsigned. `release.ps1` loads the key from `HUSHTUMBLR_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY` for the build alone, won't build a release without it, and checks the bundle came out signed by the published key. The release push gate signs its bundle with the same key, so the two still match byte for byte. The index now carries that key as `public_key`.
* **Tooling:** Device patching and the release gate know the resource ids of Tumblr 47.0 now. Rebuilding Tumblr's resource table renames four ids and rewrites one string, just as it did on 46.8, but those sit at new ids in 47.0, so every patch run stopped at the resource check after the move.
* **Tooling:** The build uses the Morphe settings plugin 2.1.0 now, which brings Kotlin 2.4.21 with it. The old plugin brought 2.4.10, which has the Kotlin build cache flaw (CVE-2026-53914), so the build had to force Kotlin up to 2.4.20 itself. That force is gone. The new plugin also signs the bundle it builds when `MORPHE_SIGNING_KEY` is set, and the release copy is still re-signed after its timestamp is pinned, so it verifies against `morphe-signing.pub` as before.
* **Tooling:** A release that stopped partway through `gh release create` picks up where it left off. The rerun checks the draft's commit, its title and tag, and every file already uploaded, sends the rest, then publishes it with fresh notes as a full release. A draft that doesn't match, an upload another run may still be sending, or a published release with the same tag gets refused before anything on GitHub changes.

patches.name: App font
patches.description: Replaces Tumblr's own font with your phone's font, or a font file you choose in settings. Fonts a post's author picked stay as they are. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Collapse long posts
patches.description: Cuts long posts in your timelines to about a screen, with Tumblr's own Read more row under them. Tap it and the whole post opens right there in the timeline. A long entry in a reblog trail gets cut the same way, and its Read more opens the post. Asks keep Tumblr's layout. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts, where you can make the cut half a screen or two screens instead.

patches.name: Dark background color
patches.description: Makes the background of Tumblr's Dark Mode palette black, which can save battery on OLED screens, or another dark color you pick when patching. On Android 12 or newer it can follow your wallpaper's colors instead. Blog and tag pages take it too, in place of their own colors. Other palettes stay as they are. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

options.description: The color the Dark Mode palette's background turns, as a six-digit color code (#RRGGBB), like #121212. Leave it blank for black. Cards get the same color and highlighted parts a slightly lighter one. Grays up to #3F3F3F work, and lighter colors are refused so text stays readable.

patches.name: Disable analytics
patches.description: Turns off Firebase and Google's analytics collection, and Tumblr's own tracking and ad measurement once it restarts. LiveRamp's identity tracker doesn't start when Tumblr launches, and Crashlytics crash reports stay off while the switch is on. The Firebase and Google analytics part stays until you patch again without it. On by default. Turn it off in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Privacy.

patches.name: Disable update prompts
patches.description: Stops Tumblr asking Google Play for a newer version and showing Play's update prompt. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Updates.

patches.name: Filter activity notifications
patches.description: Hides selected likes, reblogs, replies, follows, mentions, asks and boops from the activity list as pages load. Each switch starts off. Choose them in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Notifications.

patches.name: Fix push notifications
patches.description: Lets the patched app sign up for push notifications. Firebase can refuse a patched Tumblr whose request doesn't name Tumblr's original signature, so this sends its fingerprint. On by default. Turn it off in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Notifications.

patches.name: Hide Blaze prompts
patches.description: Hides the prompts to pay for Blaze, Tumblr's way to promote a post. That covers the Blaze buttons on your blog and dashboard, the nudge after you post, and the Blaze banners. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide Featured posts
patches.description: Takes the staff-picked posts Tumblr shows under a Featured header out of your dashboard and other feeds. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide Tumblr TV
patches.description: Takes the Tumblr TV tab out of the bottom bar, and stops sign-up from sending you there. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide Watch it rows
patches.description: Takes Tumblr TV's Watch it rows and video hub cards out of your dashboard and other feeds, along with their headings. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide ads
patches.description: Takes ad cards and paid Blaze posts out of your dashboard and other feeds. Sponsored banners go too, and a sponsored header at the top of Explore stays empty. Tumblr stops asking its ad networks for more and stops showing a full-screen ad when you open a blog, and the ad networks don't start when Tumblr launches. Its Keep Blaze posts option leaves the Blaze posts in. On by default. Turn it off in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide advertising ID
patches.description: Tumblr and the ad companies inside it see an empty advertising ID with ad tracking limited, as if you'd deleted your ad ID in Android. On by default. Turn it off in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Privacy.

patches.name: Hide blog notification reminders
patches.description: Hides the pop-up suggesting you turn on notifications for a blog. Your subscriptions and notification settings stay as they are. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide filtered posts
patches.description: Takes the posts Tumblr covers with "This post contains filtered content" out of your dashboard, searches and other feeds, so your filtered tags and words hide them completely. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide gift purchase popups
patches.description: Hides the pop-up suggesting you buy a gift for a blog. You can still open gifting yourself. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide hashtags
patches.description: Takes the tags off the bottom of posts in your dashboard, other feeds and Tumblr TV, and keeps the source link. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide liked posts
patches.description: Takes the posts you've already liked out of your dashboard as each page loads. Your likes and the rest of Tumblr still show them. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide note counts
patches.description: Takes the like, reblog and comment counts off the footer under posts, community posts included, and the counts off a post's notes, from the top and its tabs to each comment's likes and replies. The buttons stay and still work. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide photo posts
patches.description: Takes photo posts out of your dashboard and other feeds as each page loads. A post with pictures and no video, its reblog trail included, counts as a photo post. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide posts with these words
patches.description: Hides posts matching your word list. Choose whether to check current text, the reblog trail, tags or summaries. Allowed words can keep a matching post, but other enabled filters still apply. Both word editors let you type a made-up post and see what the word filter would do with it. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide reblogs
patches.description: Takes reblogs out of your dashboard and other feeds as each page loads, and keeps the posts people made themselves. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide suggested blogs
patches.description: Takes the blogs Tumblr suggests you follow out of your dashboard and other feeds, whether as cards, rows or carousels, along with their headings. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide suggested communities
patches.description: Takes the communities Tumblr suggests you join out of your dashboard and other feeds, along with their headings. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide suggested tags
patches.description: Takes the tags Tumblr suggests you follow out of your dashboard and other feeds, along with their headings. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide text posts
patches.description: Takes text posts out of your dashboard and other feeds as each page loads. A post with no pictures or video, its reblog trail included, counts as a text post. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide the Communities tab
patches.description: Takes the Communities tab out of the bottom bar and stops the Communities tips in the post editor. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide the Explore tab
patches.description: Takes the Explore and search button off the bottom bar. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide the Follow button
patches.description: Takes the Follow button out of the header of posts from blogs you don't follow yet. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide the Notifications tab
patches.description: Takes the Notifications button off the bottom bar. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide the Save button
patches.description: Takes the Save button out of the footer under posts in your dashboard and other feeds, when Tumblr shows one. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide the ad-free banner
patches.description: Hides the banner on your dashboard that asks you to pay for Ad-Free Browsing. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide the comment button
patches.description: Takes the comment button out of the footer under posts in your dashboard and other feeds. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide the diamond and TumblrMart
patches.description: Hides the Premium diamond and the TumblrMart button at the top of your dashboard, Explore and notifications. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide the like button
patches.description: Takes the like button out of the footer under posts in your dashboard and other feeds, and the reactions off community posts. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide the reblog button
patches.description: Takes the reblog button out of the footer under posts in your dashboard and other feeds. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide the share button
patches.description: Takes the share button out of the footer under posts in your dashboard and other feeds. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Hide unread dots
patches.description: Hides the unread dots and counts on the bottom bar's Dashboard, Communities and Notifications tabs, with a switch for each tab. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Hide video posts
patches.description: Takes video posts out of your dashboard and other feeds as each page loads. A post with a video anywhere in it, its reblog trail included, counts as a video post. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Hide your own reblogs
patches.description: Takes the reblogs you made out of your dashboard as each page loads. Your blog and the rest of Tumblr still show them. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: HushTumblr settings
patches.description: Adds a HushTumblr page where you turn features on or off, pause HushTumblr, back up your settings and read the licenses. Open it by long-pressing the Tumblr logo at the top of your dashboard, from Tumblr's Settings or by long-pressing the Tumblr icon. Works as soon as you patch it in, with no switch.

patches.name: Line between posts
patches.description: Draws a thin line in the gap between posts, so it's easier to see where one ends and the next begins. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Mute posts locally
patches.description: Adds a local mute action to post menus. Originals and their reblogs stay hidden for this account. On the dashboard the menu can also hide one blog's reblogs or its originals. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Feed.

patches.name: Remove ad tracking permissions
patches.description: Removes Google's advertising ID permission and Android's Privacy Sandbox ad services from Tumblr, so it can't use them. Google Play services then answers with zeros. Works as soon as you patch it in, with no switch.

patches.name: Reorder the bottom bar
patches.description: Puts the bottom bar's tabs in an order you pick, from a list in its settings. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Reveal allowed mature content
patches.description: Removes mature-content covers only when Tumblr explicitly allows them for the signed-in adult account. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Sanitize sharing links
patches.description: Links you share or copy from Tumblr leave out the ?source=share tag Tumblr adds to them, and still open the same post or blog. On by default. Turn it off in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Privacy.

patches.name: Share video links
patches.description: Long-press a video in a post to share or copy its direct link, or save the video to your phone. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Sharper images
patches.description: Loads images in posts at a higher resolution when Tumblr has a larger copy, up to twice the width Tumblr shows them at, even on a slow connection. GIFs go up too, but never past the pixel count of a 1280 by 960 one. Uses more data. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Show mutual markers
patches.description: Marks blogs that follow your primary blog when you follow them. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Show post timestamps
patches.description: Shows when posts were made using Tumblr's own timestamp layout. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

patches.name: Skip review prompts
patches.description: Stops the pop-up that asks what you think of the Tumblr app and then asks you for a store rating or feedback. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Spoof signature for Google sign-in
patches.description: Helps Google sign-in work in the patched app by naming Tumblr's original signature. It only helps with microG-RE or the XSpoofSignatures module. Email sign-in doesn't need it. It isn't selected by default. Works as soon as you patch it in, with no switch.

patches.name: Turn off screenshot sharing
patches.description: Stops Tumblr watching for screenshots, so taking one doesn't bring up its offer to save the post as an image. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Interface.

patches.name: Visible image descriptions
patches.description: Shows author-provided image descriptions below each image, including galleries and reblogs. Starts off. Turn it on in Tumblr settings > HushTumblr > Posts.

release_notes:
HushTumblr 0.0.10 has 55 patches for Tumblr 47.0.0.108. It's built on Morphe patcher 2.3.0, so it needs Morphe Manager 2.5.0 or newer.

Nine patches are new. Hide your own reblogs and Hide liked posts keep your own activity out of the dashboard, and Hide Featured posts drops the staff picks Tumblr pushes into it. Collapse long posts cuts anything longer than about a screen down to a Read more row you can open in place. Share video links, Sharper images, Line between posts, App font and Sanitize sharing links are the others, and every new switch starts off except Sanitize sharing links. Dark background color now covers blog and tag pages too and can take its color from your wallpaper. The bundle is signed from this release on, so Morphe Manager shows who signed it and won't load one signed with a different key.

Coming from 0.0.9, update Morphe Manager to 2.5.0 or newer first. Then patch Tumblr 47.0.0.108 with the default selection and install it over your current build, and your settings stay. Coming from stock Tumblr, uninstall it first, then install the patched app and sign in with your email.

## What's new

- The patches move from 46.8.1.100 to Tumblr 47.0.0.108, the newest release. Every patch applies to it, so that's the version to patch.
- The bundle is built on Morphe patcher 2.3.0 now, the one that comes with Morphe Manager 2.5.0 and Morphe Desktop 2.1.0. Update Manager to 2.5.0 or newer before you add this release, since older Manager builds can't load it.
- Dark background color now reaches blog and tag pages. Those pages paint their owner's color, so a cream blog or a teal tag used to show through the gaps between black posts. A blog's title or link color that wouldn't show on the new background turns white or near black. The screens where you edit your own blog's colors still show the real ones.
- New **Line between posts** switch on the Interface page, off by default. It draws a thin line in the gap between posts, so it's easier to see where one ends on a black background.
- New **Hide Featured posts** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes out the posts Tumblr's staff push into your dashboard under a Featured header. A post goes only when Tumblr marks it both ways, with the Featured icon and the menu choice Tumblr gives its own promotions, so a regular post with a similar header stays. Quick setups' Quiet choice turns it on too.
- New **Hide your own reblogs** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes the reblogs you made out of your dashboard, so you don't scroll past your own reblogs between the posts of people you follow. The rest of Tumblr still shows them, your blog and a post you open by itself included.
- New **Hide liked posts** switch on the Feed page, off by default. It takes posts you've already liked out of your dashboard, so the ones that come back around don't cost you scrolling. A post you like while it's on screen stays put until the feed loads it again. Everywhere else still shows them, so a liked post you open from a link or a notification is still there.
- A post you open by itself, from a link or a notification, now loads with Hide reblogs or Hide posts with words on. Those switches clear a feed, so they took out the very post you asked for and the page stayed empty. The same post in a feed later is still hidden as usual.
- New **Match my wallpaper** switch under Dark background color, off by default. On Android 12 or newer it takes the dark background from your wallpaper's colors, so there's no color code to pick when patching. A new wallpaper shows after Tumblr restarts.
- New **Share video links** switch on the Posts page, off by default. Long-press a video in a post and you can share its direct link or copy it. Before, a long press on a video did nothing at all. The same menu can also save the video into your Downloads folder, with a toast once it's in. Android 10 and newer don't ask for storage access for that. Android 8 and 9 ask first, and the save starts by itself once you allow it.
- New **Sharper images** switch on the Posts page, off by default. Tumblr loads photos in posts at 640 pixels across at most, and smaller on a slow connection, so they look soft on most phones. With the switch on, a photo loads from the larger copy Tumblr already keeps, up to twice the width it's shown at (usually the 1280 one), and a slow connection gets the same copy. It uses more data. GIFs go up too, but never past the pixel count of a 1280 by 960 one, since a playing GIF keeps a few frames in memory. Very large photos stay capped as well.
- New **Collapse long posts** switch on the Posts page, off by default. A long post can take several screens of scrolling. With the switch on, a post longer than about a screen gets cut in your timelines with Tumblr's own Read more row under it, the same one you see when an author cuts their post. Tap it and the whole post opens right where it is in the timeline, so you don't lose your place, and it stays open as you scroll on. That holds on tag pages too, where Tumblr fades long posts out by itself, so the post you opened isn't cut again there. A post Tumblr always cuts still opens on its own page. A post that runs only a little over stays whole. A long entry in a reblog trail gets cut the same way, and its Read more opens the post on its own page like an author's cut does. Asks keep Tumblr's layout. The **Collapsed post length** row under the switch moves the cut to about half a screen or two screens with a tap, and a settings file carries your pick.
- New **Sanitize sharing links** switch on the Privacy page, on by default. Tumblr adds `?source=share` to the post and blog links you share or copy, which tells it the visit came from a share. With the switch on, the link goes out without that tag and still opens the same post. A link is otherwise left exactly as Tumblr made it. Quick setups' Privacy choice turns it on too.
- Hide ads now takes sponsored banners out of your feeds too, the takeover banners a sponsor pays for and the Sponsored Day ones. Tumblr's own banners without a sponsor, like Answer Time, stay. When a sponsor has paid for the header at the top of Explore, that header stays empty instead, the same as when it doesn't load, so its takeover ad can't open from it.
- New **App font** patch, off by default. Turn it on under Interface and Tumblr's own font gives way to your phone's, or to a .ttf or .otf file you pick there. Fonts a post's author picked stay as they are, and a change shows after a restart.
- Flipping a switch near the bottom of a settings page doesn't make the page jump anymore, so a second tap in the same spot can't land on the switch next to the one you meant. Two things moved it. The restart row appearing above slid the list down, and while a switch saved, its shorter "Saving the setting" line let the rows above drop into the gap and stay there.
- Hide the Follow button now reaches the reblog trail too. Each blog quoted in a reblog has its own header with a Follow button, and those kept showing while the one at the top of the post was gone.
- The patch bundle is signed now. Morphe Manager shows "Signed by 0859 9c9b 1bd2 9cac" on the HushTumblr source and remembers that key, so a later bundle signed with any other key, or not signed at all, gets refused instead of loaded.
- Hide ads now also turns off the full-screen ad Tumblr can show when you open a blog, whether you get there from the dashboard, a reblog, a notification or a message. The pause Tumblr keeps between those ads is left alone, since switching it off would only take the pause away.
- When something in HushTumblr settings can't finish, what to do next now stays under the row you tapped. It used to be a toast that faded after a few seconds, and Android 12 and later show only two lines of one, so large text got cut off. This covers links no app can open, Android's app settings not opening, switches and tab moves that didn't save, a Resume or Quick setup that didn't run, font files that couldn't be used and refused exports or imports. The diagnostic report and **Clear diagnostic data** rows work the same way now, so the folder a full report went to stays readable. A link you can't open comes with a Copy link button.
- A failed tab move or import keeps what you tried, so trying again picks up where it stopped. The import preview also gets a **Choose another file** button for when the file itself was the problem. Notes under rows come back when Android rebuilds the screen (say, after you rotate the phone), and a result that lands after you've closed settings or switched apps shows under its row once you're back. One that lands while the screen is being rebuilt shows on the new one, and one for a row on another settings page waits there until you open it. Hiding Quick setups says right under that page's row where to get it back. A Tab order tap while a change is still saving opens the list once the save is done instead of doing nothing.
- A settings page opened with a keyboard or D-pad starts at the top again. The "HushTumblr is paused" line used to sit just above the view, so the switches under it read as on.
- With a keyboard, D-pad or mouse, the settings home page comes back where you left it after Back or a cleared search, even when a section heading or the status card sat at the top. It used to land one row further down, with that heading pushed out of view.
- A switch, font file or Quick setup that waits for a restart now says so right under that row. The note goes once you undo that change or nothing's waiting anymore, and a change the next start makes anyway (Pause while safe mode already pauses) doesn't get one. Screen readers read it once from there, and again only if you go back to it. The Tab order list shows "Saving changes" under it while a slow save runs, then where the tab went and whether Tumblr needs a restart, and the dialog keeps its size while those come and go. Android 16 is phasing out the pop-up announcements these used, and those were gone the moment they were spoken.
- Hide ads now keeps Tumblr's ad networks (Google Mobile Ads, Meta Audience Network, Vungle and Nimbus) from starting when Tumblr launches. They woke up at every cold start and wrote their files before any HushTumblr switch was read. Disable analytics does the same for LiveRamp's identity tracker. Turn either switch off, or pause HushTumblr, and they start again after a restart.
- With Hide hashtags on, a Tumblr TV video whose only text was its tags doesn't keep a lone "... more" under the blog name anymore. Tapping it opened nothing. A video with a description still gets its label.
- With Hide note counts on, each comment in a post's notes drops its own like and reply counts too, and TalkBack doesn't read them out either. The Reply and like buttons still work.
- New **Keep Blaze posts** option under Hide ads on the Feed page, off by default. With it on, posts someone paid to promote with Blaze stay in your dashboard while network ads and other sponsored cards still go. Your word and post type filters still apply to those posts.
- The Words to hide and Allowed words editors can test your list on a made-up post now. Type some post text, trail text, tags or a summary under **Try it on a post** and it tells you whether the word filter would hide that post. It names the word that did it and where it was, or the allowed word that kept the post. It uses the same whole-word matching and the same Match switches as your dashboard, and tags work typed with commas or the way a post shows them (#art #cats). Nothing typed there is saved, and it's empty again each time you open the editor.
- With **Mute posts locally** on, a post's menu on the dashboard can also hide one blog's reblogs or its originals. A reblog offers "Hide reblogs from" that blog and an original offers "Hide originals from" it, so you can keep someone's own posts while their reblogs go, or the other way around. The rule only works on your dashboard and its tabs. Explore, their blog page and search still show those posts, and so does a post you open by itself. It goes in the same private list as your muted posts, for this account only, and Manage muted posts shows it as its own row you can tap to remove. A post Tumblr doesn't say enough about to tell which kind it is always stays.
- Disable analytics now really keeps Crashlytics crash reports off. The patch already set Firebase's manifest flag for that, but Tumblr turns crash collection back on by itself every time it starts, and its call wins over the flag. With the switch on, that call now leaves collection off. Turn the switch off, or pause HushTumblr, and Tumblr's own setting is back after a restart.
- The README's Help explains how to keep a patched copy next to your regular Tumblr with Morphe's Clone app patch. You sign in to the copy with your email and it keeps its own HushTumblr settings, but `Fix push notifications` only covers the regular app.

## Behind the scenes

- The check that every GitLab mirror in a source notice still answers doesn't fail anymore when GitLab says "too many requests". It spaces its requests out, waits as long as GitLab asks (a minute at most) and tries again, so only a mirror that's really gone fails it.
- The build runs on Gradle 9.8.2 with Gson 2.15.0, Guava 33.8.0 and Commons Lang 3.21.0. None of them fixes a known advisory here, so it's upkeep. The release check accepts the 9.8.2 wrapper now.
- Device runs don't stop anymore when another session happens to read the shared lease file at the same moment. Opening or releasing the lease waits a few seconds and tries again, and a missing lease or one someone else holds still stops the run.
- The source census reads ReVanced's GitLab mirror in three GraphQL questions now. Over REST it took a request for every branch and watched path, 70 of them for that mirror's 35 branches, and GitLab allows an address with no token about 60 an hour. Each comparison is asked once a run too. Forks that GitLab has renamed while they wait to be deleted stay out of the census, because a scanner keeps making and deleting them faster than any census could record them.
- A release walk now waits for Android's verifier to finish on both the clean reference and the exact build that got installed, and both files have to hash the same before and after it runs. Publishing refuses evidence that's old or partial. It also refuses evidence that doesn't match, down to one verifier message too many or too few.
- A release walk now checks each required destination instead of trusting its screen count. Login screens, wrong search results, duplicate or missing routes, recorded problems and invalid timestamps can't earn a full PASS. Shorter exploratory walks remain partial.
- Release walks now prove which APK was installed. Patch runs keep the input, bundle, patch selection and signing identity beside the signed output. The walker checks the installed bytes before and after its run, and publishing refuses evidence that's missing or doesn't match this build.
- `scripts/walk-app.ps1` scrolls the Hush settings list with slow drags now, down first and then back up, and stops once the list stops moving. Quick swipes flung the list past rows that slid under its pinned header, so a walk on a phone could miss settings pages that were there all along.
- `scripts/patch-for-device.ps1` can now sign a gate run it reuses with the BKS key Morphe makes. Plain `apksigner.bat` can't open that keystore, so the script falls back to apksigner's own jar with BouncyCastle loaded. When both fail, the error shows what each one said.
- Changelog entries don't open with a "Tumblr:" label anymore. HushTumblr only patches Tumblr, so it repeated itself on every line. The release scripts stopped adding or asking for it, and drop it from any bullet that still has one when a release is cut.
- The build signs the bundle when `MORPHE_SIGNING_KEY` holds the private key, and refuses a key that isn't the one `morphe-signing.pub` publishes. Without it the build still works and says the bundle is unsigned. `release.ps1` loads the key from `HUSHTUMBLR_BUNDLE_SIGNING_KEY` for the build alone, won't build a release without it, and checks the bundle came out signed by the published key. The release push gate signs its bundle with the same key, so the two still match byte for byte. The index now carries that key as `public_key`.
- Device patching and the release gate know the resource ids of Tumblr 47.0 now. Rebuilding Tumblr's resource table renames four ids and rewrites one string, just as it did on 46.8, but those sit at new ids in 47.0, so every patch run stopped at the resource check after the move.
- The build uses the Morphe settings plugin 2.1.0 now, which brings Kotlin 2.4.21 with it. The old plugin brought 2.4.10, which has the Kotlin build cache flaw (CVE-2026-53914), so the build had to force Kotlin up to 2.4.20 itself. That force is gone. The new plugin also signs the bundle it builds when `MORPHE_SIGNING_KEY` is set, and the release copy is still re-signed after its timestamp is pinned, so it verifies against `morphe-signing.pub` as before.
- A release that stopped partway through `gh release create` picks up where it left off. The rerun checks the draft's commit, its title and tag, and every file already uploaded, sends the rest, then publishes it with fresh notes as a full release. A draft that doesn't match, an upload another run may still be sending, or a published release with the same tag gets refused before anything on GitHub changes.

## Reports this release answers

- #7 Colors taken from your wallpaper, and a way to use your phone's font or one you pick.
- #8 Dark background color on blog and tag pages.
- #9 Opening a reblog from a link or a notification while Hide reblogs is on.
- #10 An optional line between posts.
- #11 Sharing a video's direct link.
- #13 A switch to hide your own reblogs.

The `.mpp` download is a patch bundle, not a Tumblr APK. [Installation instructions](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTumblr#install). `SHA256SUMS.txt` is signed with the HushTumblr release key, fingerprint `2143 368A A5CE 6E5D FFEA  79CF BBC1 3768 83CF 3AB4`. [How to check a download](https://github.com/SysAdminDoc/HushTumblr#verify-a-download).

## Validation

All 1244 extension tests, 146 patch tests and 168 tests against the real Tumblr 47.0.0.108 build passed for this release, none skipped. The bundle attached here was patched onto a real Tumblr 47.0.0.108 build with Morphe's desktop patcher, and all 55 patches applied without forcing. `release-receipt-0.0.10.json` records that result, the build's hashes and what patching changed in the app's manifest.

Before release, this exact bundle patched Tumblr 47.0.0.108 for a signed-in Galaxy S22 Ultra on Android 16, and the app got a walk from end to end. It opened the dashboard, Explore, a search, a tag page, a blog, your likes, the HushTumblr settings and all ten of its pages, and Tumblr didn't crash once.
repoDescription: HushTumblr Morphe patches for Tumblr. Takes ads and clutter out of your dashboard, and much more.
